newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kidnappers have made at least seven areas in Manila their bases of operation, a crime watchdog group claims. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Some 100 heavily armed communist guerrillas attack a police detachment in Antipolo, killing a policeman and wounding another. (TODAY)
- Opposition leaders urge Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo and 11 other Cabinet members who wish to run in next year's elections to resign immediately. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Presidential aspirants of the opposition parties are being placed under intensive technical surveillance by the presidential palace, a source privy to the operations says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Philippine government has committed to rein in fiscal spending and tighten its monetary policy for the rest of the year, the International Monetary Fund says. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The public sector's external debt is likely to drop slightly to $32.13 billion this year, lower than the 1996 level of $32.86 billion, the Department of Finance says. (BUSINESS STAR)
- The Securities and Exchange Commission has allowed Victorias Milling Co to create a management committee that will oversee its operations. (TODAY)
